sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: It's the end of the year and time for our annual mini-stories episodes.
sentences.zh: 转眼又到了年底，也就是我们每年一度的迷你故事特辑时间。

sentences.en: We have three episodes this year cresting over the new year because we have so many stories.
sentences.zh: 我们今年跨年有三期节目，因为我们有太多精彩的故事了。

sentences.en: Since these are always fan favorites, I didn't think you'd mind if we stretched out a bit.
sentences.zh: 既然这些一直是粉丝的最爱，我想大家不会介意我们多聊一会儿。

sentences.en: If you're new to this, the mini-stories are a hodgepodge of fun, quick hit stories
sentences.zh: 如果你是新听众，迷你故事就是一堆有趣、节奏明快的短小故事的合集

sentences.en: that probably came up in our research for another episode, or maybe it was just some cool thing
sentences.zh: 它们可能是在我们为其他节目做调研时偶然发现的，也可能是一些很酷的事情

sentences.en: that someone told us about that we found really interesting, but we knew from doing a little
sentences.zh: 是别人告诉我们并且我们觉得非常有趣的，但我们通过一点简单的

sentences.en: bit of research they didn't warrant a full episode and two months of hard reporting and
sentences.zh: 调研就知道，它们不值得花上一整集节目以及两个月的深度报道和

sentences.en: interviews, but they're great 99PI stories nonetheless.
sentences.zh: 采访，不过它们依然是非常棒的 99PI 故事。

sentences.en: The best part, from my perspective, is that we do them as unscripted interviews where I
sentences.zh: 从我的角度来看，最棒的部分在于，我们以非正式访谈的形式来做这些节目，我可以

sentences.en: get to chat with the reporters who work on the show.
sentences.zh: 和参与节目的记者们一起闲聊。

sentences.en: Sometimes I know a little bit about what they're talking about, like we pitch them in a meeting,
sentences.zh: 有时候我对他们谈论的内容略知一二，比如我们在会议上讨论过它们的选题，

sentences.en: but sometimes I know nothing.
sentences.zh: 但有时我一无所知。

sentences.en: They keep them from me, and that's very fun.
sentences.zh: 他们对保密工作守口如瓶，这非常有趣。

sentences.en: This week, we have stories about movie novelizations, Swiss defensive architecture, Central Park
sentences.zh: 本周，我们要讲的故事包括电影小说化改编、瑞士防御工事、中央公园

sentences.en: lampposts, and the outlandish costumes of the Swedish supergroup ABBA.
sentences.zh: 路灯，以及瑞典超级乐队 ABBA 的奇特服装。

sentences.en: I mean, there's no way you can hear that list and not listen, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你听到这份清单绝对会忍不住想听下去，对吧？

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Up first is producer Chris Berube.
sentences.zh: 首先登场的是制作人克里斯·伯鲁贝。

sentences.en: So I'm here with producer Chris Berube.
sentences.zh: 所以我和制作人克里斯·伯鲁贝在这里。

sentences.en: Hey, Chris.
sentences.zh: 嘿，克里斯。

sentences.en: Hey, Roman.
sentences.zh: 嘿，罗曼。

sentences.en: How you doing?
sentences.zh: 最近怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm doing pretty good.
sentences.zh: 我挺好的。

sentences.en: How about you?
sentences.zh: 你呢？

sentences.en: I'm well.
sentences.zh: 我也很好。

sentences.en: I'm glad we are doing our mini-stories chat.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴我们能做迷你故事的闲聊。

sentences.en: I love mini-stories.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢迷你故事了。

sentences.en: It's the most wonderful time of the year, the mini-stories, partly because it is a less
sentences.zh: 这是一年中最美好的时光，也就是迷你故事特辑，部分原因在于这是一种不那么

sentences.en: formal chat with you, because I miss coming to Oakland and just having some time where
sentences.zh: 形式化的聊天，因为我很怀念去奥克兰的日子，怀念能有时间

sentences.en: we see each other in person and we can have our movie talks.
sentences.zh: 我们面对面相聚，聊聊我们喜欢的电影。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: We have to make do with movie talks on the Slack channel.
sentences.zh: 我们只能在 Slack 频道里将就着聊电影了。

sentences.en: That's called Movie.
sentences.zh: 那个频道叫“电影”。

sentences.en: What is it called?
sentences.zh: 它叫什么来着？

sentences.en: Is it Movie Club?
sentences.zh: 是叫电影俱乐部吗？

sentences.en: Movie Club.
sentences.zh: 电影俱乐部。

sentences.en: I think it is.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: It doesn't have quite the same effect.
sentences.zh: 感觉完全不一样。

sentences.en: Well, okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So I have decided to import our movie talks into mini-stories.
sentences.zh: 所以我决定把我们的电影闲聊搬到迷你故事里来。

sentences.en: Perfect.
sentences.zh: 太完美了。

sentences.en: So specifically, I want to talk about a quarantine hobby that I have taken up.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，我想聊聊我最近养成的一个隔离期爱好。

sentences.en: I've been reading a lot of movie novelizations.
sentences.zh: 我一直在读很多电影改编小说。

sentences.en: So Roman, do you remember movie novelizations?
sentences.zh: 罗曼，你还记得电影改编小说吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然记得。

sentences.en: You know, the ones I find funniest are ones that are like these action blockbusters that
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我觉得最搞笑的是那种动作大片

sentences.en: are the novelization of, I don't know, Transformers Dark Side of the Moon or something.
sentences.zh: 的小说化版本，比如，我不知道，比如《变形金刚：月黑之时》之类的。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And you think, why would anyone read that thing?
sentences.zh: 然后你会想，怎么会有人读那种东西？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对啊。

sentences.en: Speed, the official movie novelization, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 比如《生死时速》官方电影小说化，诸如此类的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全没错。

sentences.en: It's funny.
sentences.zh: 挺搞笑的。

sentences.en: There's actually this really rich history to movie novelizations.
sentences.zh: 其实电影改编小说有着非常丰富的历史。

sentences.en: So they go back to pretty much the beginning of movies.
sentences.zh: 它们的历史几乎可以追溯到电影刚诞生的时期。

sentences.en: So as soon as people started making movies, the producers realized, you know what?
sentences.zh: 因此，人们一开始拍电影，制片人们就意识到，你知道吗？

sentences.en: We could turn a quick buck if we make a book that is based on the movie.
sentences.zh: 如果我们顺便出一本根据电影改编的书，就能快速捞上一笔。

sentences.en: But they really took off in the 1970s when blockbuster films started becoming a thing.
sentences.zh: 但它们真正在上世纪 70 年代大火，当时大片开始流行起来。

sentences.en: So you had Indiana Jones and Star Wars and all these movies coming out.
sentences.zh: 所以当时有了《夺宝奇兵》、《星球大战》以及所有这些上映的电影。

sentences.en: And some of those tie-ins were actually bestsellers.
sentences.zh: 其中一些衍生小说实际上还成了畅销书。

sentences.en: Like they made the bestseller chart.
sentences.zh: 比如它们登上了畅销书排行榜。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I guess if you put yourself back in that headspace, it makes a lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你把自己带入那个年代的心态，这就完全说得通了。

sentences.en: Like back in the 70s, you had to go see a movie in a theater or not.
sentences.zh: 就像在 70 年代，你必须去电影院看电影，别无选择。

sentences.en: There was no home viewing.
sentences.zh: 当时没有家庭观影这一说。

sentences.en: Like you had to just wait until it came out on TV.
sentences.zh: 你只能干等它在电视上播出。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: Or you could get the movie novelization if you wanted to relive the movie.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你想重温电影，可以去买电影改编小说。

sentences.en: So it's kind of like if you wanted to quote unquote watch the movie at home, you bought a novelization.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像是如果你想“假装”在家看电影，你就会买一本小说来看。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Like this is the one way that you could relive it and revisit those characters and think about the movie again.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是你重温剧情、重回角色身边并再次回味电影的唯一途径。

sentences.en: That actually makes a ton of sense.
sentences.zh: 这其实非常合乎情理。

sentences.en: I like that.
sentences.zh: 我挺喜欢这个概念的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But that doesn't explain in this moment of streaming every type of video content that's ever existed why you are reading them right now.
sentences.zh: 但这并不能解释，在如今这个流媒体几乎涵盖了人类有史以来所有视频内容的时代，你为什么现在还要去读它们。

sentences.en: True.
sentences.zh: 也对。

sentences.en: I could watch Star Wars.
sentences.zh: 我可以看《星球大战》。

sentences.en: If I wanted to watch Star Wars, that option is available to me.
sentences.zh: 如果我想看《星球大战》，这个选项是现成的。

sentences.en: So I started getting really interested in these because of the generic product episode that we made.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始对这些产生浓厚兴趣，是因为我们之前制作的那期关于“无品牌商品”的节目。

sentences.en: So do you remember the generic branding episode?
sentences.zh: 所以你还记得无品牌包装那期节目吗？

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然记得。

sentences.en: It's an instant classic.
sentences.zh: 那是一期瞬间成为经典的节目。

sentences.en: Everyone loved it.
sentences.zh: 大家都非常喜欢。

sentences.en: Especially your Canadian brethren.
sentences.zh: 特别是你的加拿大同胞们。

sentences.en: It was the most Canadian episode of 99PI we've had.
sentences.zh: 那是我们做过的最具加拿大风情的一期 99PI 节目。

sentences.en: So you may recall one of the people we spoke to for that episode was a guy named Terry Bisson, who was the editor of this series of generic books.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得，我们那期节目采访的人之一叫特里·比森，他是这套无品牌书籍系列的编辑。

sentences.en: This was like a footnote in the story.
sentences.zh: 这在故事里只是个微不足道的脚注。

sentences.en: Yeah, but it's a very memorable footnote.
sentences.zh: 对，但这是一个让人印象深刻的脚注。

sentences.en: It totally is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So just to refresh your memory, here's Terry talking about the No Frills books that he helped edit.
sentences.zh: 所以为了帮你恢复记忆，这里是特里谈论他曾协助编辑的无标牌系列书籍。

sentences.en: I thought of it as a satire on publishing.
sentences.zh: 我把它看作是对出版业的一种讽刺。

sentences.en: If you could have No Frills Corn Flakes, why couldn't you have a No Frills romance?
sentences.zh: 既然可以有无品牌玉米片，为什么不能有无品牌言情小说呢？

sentences.en: So I did this interview with Terry, and we're talking, and he's actually this really fascinating guy.
sentences.zh: 我和特里做了这次采访，我们聊了起来，他其实是一个非常迷人的人。

sentences.en: So he's a really well-regarded sci-fi writer, and we were talking about his career, and he mentions that for a while,
sentences.zh: 他是一位备受推崇的科幻小说家，我们聊到了他的职业生涯，他提到有一段时间，

sentences.en: he used to write movie novelizations as a way to make some cash.
sentences.zh: 他曾经靠写电影小说化来赚点外快。

sentences.en: So he did some pretty big movies, actually, like Johnny Mnemonic, the Keanu Reeves movie.
sentences.zh: 所以他实际上写过一些相当大制作的电影，比如基努·里维斯主演的《捍卫机密》。

sentences.en: He did Galaxy QueSt.
sentences.zh: 他还写过《惊异大奇航》。

sentences.en: He did a Bruce Willis sci-fi movie that you may remember called The Fifth Element.
sentences.zh: 他写过一部你可能还记得的布鲁斯·威利斯科幻电影，叫做《第五元素》。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然记得。

sentences.en: And you remember that movie.
sentences.zh: 你还记得那部电影。

sentences.en: It was about 95 or something like that when it came out.
sentences.zh: 它上映的时候大概是 95 年左右吧。

sentences.en: And it sold really well.
sentences.zh: 而且它卖得非常好。

sentences.en: I think the reason it sold was because people thought, well,
sentences.zh: 我想它之所以卖得好，是因为人们觉得，嗯，

sentences.en: maybe the book will explain what's going on in the movie because there was a lot of stuff in the movie that didn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 也许这本书能解释电影里到底发生了什么，因为电影里有很多让人摸不着头脑的东西。

sentences.en: And they thought maybe I would make sense out of it.
sentences.zh: 他们以为我能把这些理出个头绪来。

sentences.en: But I didn't even try.
sentences.zh: 但我根本没试过。

sentences.en: So I'm talking to Terry.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时在和特里聊天。

sentences.en: We're talking about his career.
sentences.zh: 我们正在谈论他的职业生涯。

sentences.en: And I'm saying, wow, it's really cool that you got to see these movies before anybody else.
sentences.zh: 我说，哇，能比任何人都先看到这些电影，真是太酷了。

sentences.en: And Terry tells me something really surprising.
sentences.zh: 然后特里告诉我一件非常让人意外的事。

sentences.en: And that is he never saw the movies.
sentences.zh: 那就是他从来没看过那些电影。

sentences.en: Well, that is surprising.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这确实让人意外。

sentences.en: How is that possible?
sentences.zh: 这怎么可能？

sentences.en: Well, he might have seen the movie after it came out, but he didn't get to see the movie while he was writing the book.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他可能在电影上映后看过，但在写书的时候他可没机会看。

sentences.en: It's usually done while the movie is either still being done or is in post-production.
sentences.zh: 这项工作通常是在电影还在制作中或者处于后期制作阶段时完成的。

sentences.en: And at the last minute, they thought, look, we'll spend 20 grand and it promotes the movie a little bit.
sentences.zh: 而在最后一分钟，他们会想，听着，我们花两万美元就能对电影起到一点宣传作用。

sentences.en: So because of the production schedules, Terry said in his experience, it was always based off the script and not the actual movie when you're doing the novelization.
sentences.zh: 所以由于制作日程的安排，特里说根据他的经验，当你进行小说化创作时，内容永远是基于剧本而不是实际的电影。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I mean, I guess that makes sense now that you lay it out.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，经你这么一说，这倒也合情合理。

sentences.en: But it is truly weird to think about that these novelizations haven't connected to the actual visual part of the movie at all.
sentences.zh: 但一想到这些小说化作品与电影的实际视觉部分完全没有关联，就真的觉得很诡异。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I was actually like a little bit skeptical when he told me this.
sentences.zh: 他刚告诉我的时候，我其实还带着一丝怀疑。

sentences.en: I'm like, how do you write a novelization of a movie with no movie?
sentences.zh: 我在想，没看电影怎么写得出电影的小说化作品？

sentences.en: So Terry, after we had our generics talk, he connected me with a friend of his named Liz Hand, who's another sci-fi writer who wrote a number of these novelizations.
sentences.zh: 所以特里在和我们聊完无品牌商品后，把我介绍给了他的朋友莉兹·汉德，她也是一位写过好几部这类小说的科幻作家。

sentences.en: And she pretty much confirmed everything that Terry said.
sentences.zh: 她几乎证实了特里所说的一切。

sentences.en: Like she did 12 Monkeys.
sentences.zh: 比如她写过《十二猴子》。

sentences.en: She did the X-Files movie.
sentences.zh: 她写过《X档案》电影版。

sentences.en: And she said, yeah, all you ever get is the script.
sentences.zh: 她说，没错，你唯一能拿到的就是剧本。

sentences.en: I did six or seven novelizations.
sentences.zh: 我写过六七部小说化作品。

sentences.en: And with one exception, I know did not see a film.
sentences.zh: 除了其中一次例外，我知道自己确实没看过电影。

sentences.en: As you've been reading these and doing a little bit of this research, what does it mean for the person writing the novelization to have not seen the movie?
sentences.zh: 在你阅读这些书并做了一点相关调研的过程中，对于写小说的人来说，没看过电影究竟意味着什么？

sentences.en: So what it means is that the novelization will have a lot of detail that is different from the movie because of how movies are made.
sentences.zh: 这意味着由于电影拍摄的方式，小说化版本会有很多与电影不同的细节。

sentences.en: So think about it.
sentences.zh: 所以你想想看。

sentences.en: I mean, part of the issue is that stuff will change from the script while you're making the movie.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，问题的一部分在于，在拍电影的过程中，有些东西会偏离剧本。

sentences.en: So, you know, an actor comes up with a new line or some special effects are too expensive to film.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，演员临场发挥了一句新台词，或者某些特效拍起来太贵了。

sentences.en: Terry was telling me, actually, when he was writing the Galaxy Quest book, they kept changing the ending.
sentences.zh: 特里告诉我，实际上当他在写《惊异大奇航》这本书时，他们一直在改结局。

sentences.en: They kept rewriting the damn script.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在重写该死的剧本。

sentences.en: And they probably had these groups that told them what ending they liked and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 而且他们可能还有那些焦点小组来告诉他们喜欢哪个结局之类的。

sentences.en: I had to rewrite the last 10, 15 pages of it three or four times.
sentences.zh: 我不得不把最后 10 到 15 页重写了三四遍。

sentences.en: What Terry's describing, which is like he would go back in and rewrite it to match the movie, that was kind of rare.
sentences.zh: 特里所描述的那种情况，也就是他会回去重写以配合电影，其实挺罕见的。

sentences.en: That often did not happen.
sentences.zh: 这种情况通常不会发生。

sentences.en: So with a lot of these novelizations, changes got made and the producers just wouldn't bother to tell the writer who's doing the novel.
sentences.zh: 所以在很多这类小说化作品中，改动已经发生了，而制片人根本懒得去通知写小说的作家。

sentences.en: So there's all of these examples of movie novelizations where there are details that are wrong compared to the movie.
sentences.zh: 所以有各种各样的电影小说化作品，里面的细节与电影相比都是错的。

sentences.en: So, Roman, for example, I assume you've seen E.T., the extraterrestrial.
sentences.zh: 所以，罗曼，比如说，我猜你看过《E.T.外星人》吧。

sentences.en: Sure, I did.
sentences.zh: 当然，我看过。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: One of the most popular movies ever.
sentences.zh: 有史以来最受欢迎的电影之一。

sentences.en: Now, you remember there's a scene in E.T.
sentences.zh: 现在，你还记得《E.T.》里的那个场景吗？

sentences.en: where Elliot, the little kid, is trying to lure out E.T.
sentences.zh: 小男孩埃利奥特试图引诱外星人现身

sentences.en: and he's using candy.
sentences.zh: 他用的诱饵是糖果。

sentences.en: With the Reese's Pieces, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，就是里斯花生酱杯糖果（Reese's Pieces）。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's super famous.
sentences.zh: 对，超级出名。

sentences.en: So in the novel, it's M&M's because they hadn't struck a deal with Reese's Pieces yet.
sentences.zh: 所以在小说里，糖果写的是M&M's，因为他们当时还没和里斯谈好合作。

sentences.en: So another example is The Empire Strikes Back, the novelization of that.
sentences.zh: 另一个例子是《帝国反击战》，它的同名小说。

sentences.en: In the novel, Yoda is blue.
sentences.zh: 在小说里，尤达是蓝色的。

sentences.en: If you had to describe Yoda, first thing you say is he's a green dude, like he's Hall of Fame green thing.
sentences.zh: 如果你要描述尤达，你首先会说他是个绿色的家伙，简直是绿色的典范。

sentences.en: If there was a Hall of Fame for stuff that is green, Yoda would be in there on the first ballot, I think.
sentences.zh: 如果有一个绿色事物的名人堂，我觉得尤达绝对能首轮入选。

sentences.en: Absolutely, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对的，绝对的。

sentences.en: So that thing happens quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 所以这种事挺常见的。

sentences.en: There were like small changes that would get made.
sentences.zh: 会有一些细微的改动。

sentences.en: And ultimately, you know, that doesn't really ruin the experience of reading the book if it's still the same story.
sentences.zh: 而且说到底，你知道的，只要故事还是那个故事，这并不会真的毁掉阅读小说的体验。

sentences.en: The other problem, though, is that screenplays aren't very detailed.
sentences.zh: 不过另一个问题是，电影剧本其实写得很简略。

sentences.en: So when you're reading a screenplay, there's just like a lot of gaps.
sentences.zh: 所以当你读剧本时，会发现里面有很多空白。

sentences.en: The screenplays are like 120 pages, basically, of material, and it's all dialogue with a few set directions.
sentences.zh: 剧本基本上也就120页左右的篇幅，全都是对话，外加一点场景指导。

sentences.en: You need a lot of filler.
sentences.zh: 你需要大量的填充内容。

sentences.en: In a screenplay, it might say the characters walk into a room and you don't get any other details.
sentences.zh: 在剧本里，可能只会写角色走进一个房间，然后你就没有任何其他细节了。

sentences.en: So if you're the person writing the novelization, you have to fill in all these details of what the room looks like or what the characters are wearing,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是小说化改编的创作者，你就必须自己填补所有这些细节，比如房间长什么样，角色穿着什么，

sentences.en: all these things you don't have access to.
sentences.zh: 所有这些你原本无法得知的信息。

sentences.en: And sometimes the screenplay doesn't have details of very important stuff.
sentences.zh: 而且有时剧本甚至没有包含非常重要的事情的细节。

sentences.en: So, Roman, one of my favorite movies is Alien, as you know.
sentences.zh: 罗曼，你知道的，我的最爱之一就是电影《异形》。

sentences.en: Sure, it's great.
sentences.zh: 当然，太棒了。

sentences.en: It's one of the beSt.
sentences.zh: 它是最顶尖的之一。

sentences.en: Here's something that's funny about the screenplay for Alien.
sentences.zh: 关于《异形》的剧本，有一件很有趣的事。

sentences.en: They don't describe the alien.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没有描述异形长什么样。

sentences.en: So what did they do when they had to do the novelization?
sentences.zh: 那他们在写小说时该怎么办呢？

sentences.en: So I found this old article about Alan Dean Foster, who wrote the novelization, and he says he went to the studio and was like, hey, can I see the alien?
sentences.zh: 我找到了一篇关于阿兰·迪恩·福斯特（Alan Dean Foster）的旧文章，他是那本小说的作者，他说他曾去过制片厂，问对方：“嘿，我能看看异形吗？”

sentences.en: And they said no.
sentences.zh: 然后他们说不行。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So what did he do?
sentences.zh: 那他怎么办？

sentences.en: Well, there's a lot of passages in the novelization where you could see he's clearly trying to avoid getting specific about it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在小说里有很多段落，你能看出他明显在极力避免具体描述它。

sentences.en: So here's one.
sentences.zh: 所以这是其中一段。

sentences.en: There was a vague suggestion of something tall and heavy.
sentences.zh: “有一个高大而沉重的模糊暗示。”

sentences.en: This is a bit later on.
sentences.zh: 这是稍微靠后一点的剧情。

sentences.en: Above the helpless figure was a faint outline.
sentences.zh: “在这个无助的身影上方，有一个隐约的轮廓。”

sentences.en: Something man-shaped, but definitely not a man.
sentences.zh: “某种人形的东西，但绝对不是人。”

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: There's some real verbal gymnastics to not be specific there.
sentences.zh: 为了避免具体描述，这里真的做了一番语言体操。

sentences.en: That's pretty good, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实写得挺好的。

sentences.en: And that novelization of Alien is seen as a classic of the genre.
sentences.zh: 而且《异形》的那本小说被视为同类题材中的经典。

sentences.en: It was an actual bestseller.
sentences.zh: 它曾经是一本真正的畅销书。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But there are some cases where the writer is trying to fill in these details and add things and gets a little carried away, maybe.
sentences.zh: 但有些情况下，作家在试图填补这些细节并添加内容时，可能有点得意忘形了。

sentences.en: Give me an example of that.
sentences.zh: 给我举个例子吧。

sentences.en: So an example of this that's pretty notorious is Jaws the Revenge, the fourth Jaws movie.
sentences.zh: 一个挺出名的例子就是《大白鲨4：复仇》（Jaws the Revenge），《大白鲨》系列的第四部电影。

sentences.en: And the writer added this whole backstory about why the shark in Jaws keeps chasing the same family.
sentences.zh: 作者在里面加了一整段背景故事，解释为什么《大白鲨》里的鲨鱼一直在追杀同一个家庭。

sentences.en: And the explanation is a voodoo curse.
sentences.zh: 而这个解释竟然是巫术诅咒。

sentences.en: I think in Jaws the Revenge, the shark follows Ellen Brody down to the Bahamas or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我想在《大白鲨4：复仇》里，鲨鱼一路追着艾伦·布罗迪（Ellen Brody）到了巴哈马或者诸如此类的地方。

sentences.en: Yeah, that is what happens.
sentences.zh: 对，剧情确实是这样的。

sentences.en: And clearly the person writing the novelization took some inspiration.
sentences.zh: 很显然，写小说的这个人获得了一些灵感。

sentences.en: This is a leap in logic that's a little too far, so I have to do something to explain it.
sentences.zh: 这个逻辑跨度有点太大了，所以我必须做点什么来解释它。

sentences.en: So ancient curse is the easiest way to connect those dots.
sentences.zh: 所以远古诅咒是把这些点连起来最简单的方法。

sentences.en: It makes as much sense as anything else.
sentences.zh: 反正它跟其他解释一样离谱。

sentences.en: And this kind of thing would happen when you were writing and, you know, you hit a book where you didn't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 当你写作时，你知道的，遇到一本让你不知所措的书，这种事就会发生。

sentences.en: And Liz Hand gave me an example from her career where she had to do this.
sentences.zh: 莉兹·汉德（Liz Hand）就跟我分享过她职业生涯中不得不这么做的一个例子。

sentences.en: I won't say that, you know, the novelization of Catwoman is my finest moment, but it was a paycheck.
sentences.zh: 我不会说《猫女》的小说化是我职业生涯的高光时刻，但它确实是一份收入。

sentences.en: Does she mean the Halle Berry movie, Catwoman?
sentences.zh: 她指的是哈莉·贝瑞演的那部电影《猫女》吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So the Halle Berry Catwoman, kind of a notorious flop.
sentences.zh: 所以哈莉·贝瑞演的《猫女》，可以说是出了名的惨败。

sentences.en: I think it still has 9% on Rotten Tomatoes, last I checked.
sentences.zh: 我上次查的时候，它在烂番茄上好像还有9%的好评率。

sentences.en: Rough, yeah.
sentences.zh: 太惨了，是的。

sentences.en: What can I do for you?
sentences.zh: 有什么需要我效劳的吗？

sentences.en: White Russian.
sentences.zh: 白俄罗斯鸡尾酒（White Russian）。

sentences.en: No ice.
sentences.zh: 不要冰。

sentences.en: Hold the vodka.
sentences.zh: 不加伏特加。

sentences.en: Hold the Kahlua.
sentences.zh: 不加卡鲁瓦咖啡利口酒。

sentences.en: Green.
sentences.zh: 绿色。

sentences.en: Straight up.
sentences.zh: 纯饮。

sentences.en: Liz was given the script for this and she looks at it and she realizes, oh no, like this is a mess.
sentences.zh: 莉兹拿到了这个剧本，她看了一遍然后意识到，天哪，这简直是一团糟。

sentences.en: Like, what am I going to do?
sentences.zh: 心想，我该怎么办？

sentences.en: There's very little detail in here.
sentences.zh: 这里面的细节太少了。

sentences.en: How am I going to fill a book?
sentences.zh: 我怎么才能撑起一本书的篇幅呢？

sentences.en: So then how did she solve this problem?
sentences.zh: 那她是怎么解决这个问题的？

sentences.en: So get ready.
sentences.zh: 准备好了吗。

sentences.en: The way she solved this problem is kind of amazing.
sentences.zh: 她解决这个问题的方式简直绝了。

sentences.en: So what I ended up doing, there was a character in the book, in the screenplay rather, who was a supporting character, who was like a renowned catologist,
sentences.zh: 我最后做的是，书里——准确地说是剧本里——有一个配角，是一个著名的猫类学家，

sentences.en: a supposed anthropologist, archaeologist who specialized in cats.
sentences.zh: 一个专门研究猫的伪人类学家、考古学家。

sentences.en: And the cat woman character would go periodically to visit this woman to ask for, you know, oh, help me, OB cat, tell me what to do with my little pointy ears.
sentences.zh: 猫女这个角色会定期去拜访这个女人寻求帮助，你知道的，“噢，猫女士帮帮我，告诉我该怎么处理我那尖尖的小耳朵。”

sentences.en: And so what I thought was like, okay, I know what I can do, even though this is totally out of line.
sentences.zh: 所以当时我想的是，好吧，我知道我能做什么，尽管这完全不合常规。

sentences.en: I'm just going to do it anyway.
sentences.zh: 管他呢，我还是要这么做。

sentences.en: So I wrote three or four little cat, I made up three or four little cat fables or fairy tales.
sentences.zh: 所以我写了三四个关于猫的小故事，我自己编了三四个猫的寓言或童话。

sentences.en: And so each time the cat woman character would go to see this woman, the action ground to a halt.
sentences.zh: 所以每次猫女去见这个女人时，情节的发展就会停顿下来。

sentences.en: I dropped these things in and basically they were filler, but for me, they were fun.
sentences.zh: 我把这些内容塞了进去，基本上它们就是填充物，但对当时的我觉得挺有意思的。

sentences.en: And actually one of these folk tales that Liz wrote turned out so well that she managed to get it published in a couple of short story anthologies,
sentences.zh: 事实上，莉兹写的这些民间故事之一效果出奇地好，以至于她设法把它发表在了几本短篇小说选集里，

sentences.en: including this one anthology of stories about cats, where it's a story by Stephen King, a story by George R.R.
sentences.zh: 其中包括一本关于猫的故事选集，里面有斯蒂芬·金（Stephen King）的故事，乔治·R·R·

sentences.en: Martin, and then also her short story that was originally in the Catwoman novelization.
sentences.zh: 马丁（George R.R. Martin）的故事，还有她那篇原本写进《猫女》小说里的小短篇。

sentences.en: That is so good.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: It's really funny.
sentences.zh: 真的很有趣。

sentences.en: I mean, it's so interesting because a couple months ago, you know, I probably had the same thoughts that you did about movie novelizations.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太有意思了，因为几个月前，你知道的，我可能跟你有着相同的看法，对电影同名小说不屑一顾。

sentences.en: I thought, oh, yeah, these are cash ins.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，噢，对，这些就是为了捞钱的玩意儿。

sentences.en: These kind of seem like hack work.
sentences.zh: 这些看起来像是粗制滥造的行活儿。

sentences.en: But the deeper you dig into them, the more you realize there's creativity here.
sentences.zh: 但你越是深入挖掘，就越会发现其中蕴含的创造力。

sentences.en: They're kind of weird.
sentences.zh: 它们有点奇特。

sentences.en: They're kind of their own thing from the movies.
sentences.zh: 它们在电影之外形成了独特的存在。

sentences.en: And to me, that's a really interesting way to think about the original movie.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这是一种思考原版电影的非常有趣的方式。

sentences.en: And it kind of deepens the whole experience of being a fan.
sentences.zh: 它在某种程度上加深了作为粉丝的整体体验。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of beautiful.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直太美妙了。

sentences.en: I really love it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢这种感觉

sentences.en: Like people operating with your creativity and the sort of marginalia of this gigantic, you know, creative apparatus.
sentences.zh: 就像人们在运用你的创造力，围绕着这个庞大无比的创意机器做一些边缘创作。

sentences.en: It's so cool.
sentences.zh: 太酷了。

sentences.en: I have a few special thank yous.
sentences.zh: 我有几位要特别感谢的人。

sentences.en: Before we go, I want to thank my brother, Dan, who is a big fan of these novelizations.
sentences.zh: 在节目结束前，我要感谢我的兄弟丹，他是这些小说的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: He gave me some great advice for this story.
sentences.zh: 他为这个故事给了我很多极好的建议。

sentences.en: Also, thank you to Justin Morris, who gave me a great list of things to read to learn more about this.
sentences.zh: 还要感谢贾斯汀·莫里斯（Justin Morris），他给我列了一大串书单，让我能深入了解这方面的知识。

sentences.en: And thank you to the authors who are very serious science fiction writers who indulged me and were very generous with their time talking about these footnotes in their careers.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢那些非常严肃的科幻小说作家，他们包容了我，并且非常慷慨地抽出时间跟我聊聊他们职业生涯中的这些脚注。

sentences.en: So thank you to Terry Bisson, Oakland's own Terry Bisson.
sentences.zh: 所以要感谢特里·比森（Terry Bisson），奥克兰本土的特里·比森。

sentences.en: And thank you very much to Liz Hand, her new book.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢莉兹·汉德，她的新书。

sentences.en: It's a novel called The Book of Lamps and Banners.
sentences.zh: 那是一部名为《灯具与横幅之书》（The Book of Lamps and Banners）的小说。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: One of the stories that came over the transom via Twitter this year is about the four-digit codes on the lampposts in Central Park in New York City.
sentences.zh: 今年通过推特（Twitter）传入我们视线的故事之一，讲的是纽约中央公园路灯杆上的四位数字编码。

sentences.en: A person named Gloria at Lucent 508 tweeted about this clever form of wayfinding in the park.
sentences.zh: 一个叫格洛丽亚（Gloria）的用户在@Lucent 508上发推文介绍了公园里这种巧妙的寻路方式。

sentences.en: And I think like a hundred people said it to me.
sentences.zh: 我想大概有一百个人把这事发给我了。

sentences.en: So each lamppost in the park has a four-digit number on it.
sentences.zh: 公园里的每根路灯杆上都有一个四位数编号。

sentences.en: The first two digits represent the closest cross street to the post in the 840-acre city park.
sentences.zh: 在这座占地840英亩的城市公园里，前两位数字代表着距离路灯杆最近的横街。

sentences.en: So if the first two digits are 96, the post is parallel to 96th Street.
sentences.zh: 所以如果前两位数字是96，说明这根灯杆与96街平行。

sentences.en: The second two digits represent two things.
sentences.zh: 后两位数字代表两件事情。

sentences.en: Which side the lamppost is on and its relative distance from the edge.
sentences.zh: 路灯杆位于哪一侧，以及它距离边缘的相对距离。

sentences.en: If it is an even number, then it's on the east side of the park.
sentences.zh: 如果是个偶数，那么它就在公园的东侧。

sentences.en: So E-even, E-eaSt.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，E代表偶数（Even），E代表东侧（East）。

sentences.en: That's how I remember that.
sentences.zh: 我是这么记住的。

sentences.en: And an odd number means that that light is closer to the west side.
sentences.zh: 如果是奇数，则意味着这盏灯更靠近西侧。

sentences.en: The smaller the number, the closer it is to the edge.
sentences.zh: 数字越小，说明它离边缘越近。

sentences.en: So for example, 9605 is roughly parallel to 96th Street.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，9605大致与96街平行。

sentences.en: And it's pretty close to the west side because it has a small, odd number.
sentences.zh: 而且它离西侧很近，因为它是一个较小的奇数。

sentences.en: But if a lamppost is numbered 9642, it's closer to the east side than it is to the west side.
sentences.zh: 但如果一根灯杆的编号是9642，它比西侧更靠近东侧。

sentences.en: But because it has that high number, 42, it's more towards the middle of the park.
sentences.zh: 但由于它的尾数是个较大的数字42，所以它更朝向公园的中间位置。

sentences.en: So if you ever get lost in Central Park, find a lamppost, read the embossed number, and you'll know roughly where you are.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在中央公园迷路了，找一根路灯杆，读一读上面压印的数字，你就能大致知道自己在哪儿了。

sentences.en: When the explanation for this code, you know, found people on the internet, a lot of people were intrigued by it.
sentences.zh: 当这个编码的解释在互联网上流传开来时，很多人都对此感到好奇。

sentences.en: But they often wondered, well, what good is this cool wayfinding method if nobody knows about it?
sentences.zh: 但他们通常会想，如果根本没人知道，那这个酷炫的寻路方法又有什么用呢？

sentences.en: Well, the answer is, it's not really wayfinding for us, for patrons of the park.
sentences.zh: 嗯，答案是，这其实不是给我们这些公园游客准备的寻路方式。

sentences.en: It's really for park employees whose job it is to replace and repair those lamps.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是为公园员工准备的，他们的工作就是更换和修理这些路灯。

sentences.en: But now that you know, you could like spin around with a blindfold on, set off in any direction, find a lamp, and know where you are in Central Park, which is pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 但既然你现在知道了，你就可以蒙上眼睛原地转圈，然后随便挑个方向出发，找到一盏路灯，就能知道自己在中央公园的什么位置，这其实挺酷的。

sentences.en: Up next is the digital director of 99PI and the co-author of The 99% Invisible City, Kurt Kolstad.
sentences.zh: 接下来这位是99PI的数字总监兼《99%隐形城市》（The 99% Invisible City）的合著者库尔特·科尔斯特ッド（Kurt Kolstad）。

sentences.en: So if you know anything about the history of Switzerland, you probably know that it's a beautiful mountainous country.
sentences.zh: 如果你对瑞士的历史有所了解，你大概知道这是一个美丽的山地国家。

sentences.en: And it has famously remained as neutral as possible when it comes to global conflicts.
sentences.zh: 而且众所周知，在面对全球冲突时，它一直保持着尽可能中立的立场。

sentences.en: Kurt Kolstad is here to talk about how that stance has shaped the built environment of Switzerland, including, you know, kind of obvious ways,
sentences.zh: 库尔特·科尔斯特ッド今天来这里跟我们聊聊，这种立场是如何塑造瑞士的建筑环境的，包括那些显而易见的方式，

sentences.en: but also really strange and furtive ways as well.
sentences.zh: 以及一些非常奇特且隐蔽的方式。

sentences.en: Yes, Switzerland is filled with defensive architecture and infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 没错，瑞士到处都是防御性的建筑和基础设施。

sentences.en: And yes, some of it is pretty obvious.
sentences.zh: 是的，其中有一些相当明显。

sentences.en: Like on the tops of some hills and mountains, you can find these rows of jagged concrete teeth just sticking up from the ground.
sentences.zh: 比如在一些山丘和山峰的顶端，你能看到一排排锯齿状的混凝土“牙齿”从地面突出来。

sentences.en: And some people call them Toblerone lines.
sentences.zh: 有些人把它们称为大理石巧克力防线（Toblerone lines）。

sentences.en: Like the chocolate.
sentences.zh: 就像那种巧克力一样。

sentences.en: Is that the, is that, that's another thing that Switzerland is famous for is that spiky chocolate.
sentences.zh: 那是，那是，瑞士闻名遐迩的另一种东西就是那种三角形的巧克力。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And it's because of that, you know, jagged shape.
sentences.zh: 正是因为那种，你知道的，锯齿状的形状。

sentences.en: Uh, but these are built up to stop incoming tanks from rolling over hillsides into Swiss territory.
sentences.zh: 呃，但这些建筑修筑起来是为了阻止敌方坦克从山坡上开进瑞士领土。

sentences.en: So these like literally look like if you were to take one of those chocolate bars out of its package, it's a piece of concrete,
sentences.zh: 所以这些东西字面意思上看起来就像，如果你把其中一块巧克力从包装里拿出来，它就是一块混凝土，

sentences.en: a big piece of concrete that just looks just like a Toblerone.
sentences.zh: 一大块混凝土，长得就像三角巧克力一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, basically.
sentences.zh: 对，基本上是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So that's an example of a, you know, a kind of an obvious defensive design.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是一个，你知道的，某种显而易见的防御性设计的例子。

sentences.en: What's it, what's a more invisible design?
sentences.zh: 那什么是，什么更隐蔽的设计？

sentences.en: Well, I'll start with the one that sent me down this whole rabbit hole.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我从让我陷入这一切深渊的那个开始讲起。

sentences.en: So a few years back, the Swiss government decided to remove some explosives from an old bridge and that made the news.
sentences.zh: 所以几年前，瑞士政府决定从一座老桥上拆除一些炸药，这上了新闻。

sentences.en: So wait, so they actually had explosives built into the bridge itself.
sentences.zh: 等等，所以他们实际上在桥体本身里面内置了炸药。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that was my reaction to, I understand the same question.
sentences.zh: 这也是我的反应，我理解有同样疑问的人。

sentences.en: I was like, why, why would you rig your own bridge with explosives?
sentences.zh: 我当时想，为什么，你为什么要给自己的桥梁装上炸药？

sentences.en: And the bridging question is an old one.
sentences.zh: 而关于桥梁的问题是一个古老的问题。

sentences.en: It's 700 plus years old.
sentences.zh: 它有七百多年的历史了。

sentences.en: But during the cold war, they strapped TNT to this thing so that key supports could be detonated in case of invasion.
sentences.zh: 但在冷战期间，他们在这东西绑上了TNT，以便在遭到入侵时可以引爆关键支撑结构。

sentences.en: Okay, so they removed those.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以他们把那些拆除了。

sentences.en: Is that tactic no longer a thing in Switzerland?
sentences.zh: 这种战术在瑞士现在已经没有了吗？

sentences.en: Well, here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，情况是这样的。

sentences.en: Switzerland won't actually comment on that for security reasons.
sentences.zh: 出于安全原因，瑞士实际上不会对此发表评论。

sentences.en: So it's possible that they're just done with that.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能只是不再这么做了。

sentences.en: But it's also possible they just swapped it out with new explosives.
sentences.zh: 但也有可能他们只是换成了新型炸药。

sentences.en: And this is just one part of the equation, right?
sentences.zh: 而这只是整个局面的冰山一角，对吧？

sentences.en: So some bridges are also flanked with artillery, which is like hidden in the mountainside and works as like a backup system.
sentences.zh: 所以有些桥梁旁边还部署了火炮，这些火炮藏在山腰里，作为一种备用系统。

sentences.en: So they can retreat.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就可以撤退。

sentences.en: And then if the enemy tries to repair the bridge, the Swiss can just rain fire down on them and stop them from doing it.
sentences.zh: 然后如果敌人试图修复桥梁，瑞士人就可以向他们倾泻火力，阻止他们这么做。

sentences.en: And so all of this is a way to like keep the enemies, you know, both from crossing the bridge and then from fixing the bridge in case they want to come back across.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些都是为了让敌人，你知道的，既无法过桥，也无法在他们想过桥时修复桥梁。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So they got explosives to detonate the bridge and guns pointed down at them in case the enemy wants to repair that bridge if it's been detonated.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有炸药可以炸毁桥梁，如果在桥梁被炸毁后敌人想修复它，还有枪支居高临下地瞄准他们。

sentences.en: So they have all kinds of things in their arsenal.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的武器库里有各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: Yes, totally.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: And secrecy and redundancy are a huge part of that.
sentences.zh: 而保密和冗余是其中非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: And bridges are also just a small part of that.
sentences.zh: 桥梁也只是其中的一小部分。

sentences.en: So in the Alps, for example, the government has carved out tens of thousands of bunkers and other installations over the decades.
sentences.zh: 所以在阿尔卑斯山，举个例子，几十年来政府开凿了数万个掩体和其他设施。

sentences.en: And they've also rigged explosives up in the mountains to trigger landslides.
sentences.zh: 他们还在山里安装了炸药来引发山体滑坡。

sentences.en: Again, a way of, you know, stopping or at least slowing down would be invaders.
sentences.zh: 同样，这也是阻止或至少减缓潜在入侵者的一种方式。

sentences.en: And then there are those little villages and, you know, the ones I'm talking about, you see them on postcards.
sentences.zh: 然后还有那些小村庄，你知道的，我说的是明信片上能看到的那种。

sentences.en: So you mean like these Swiss hill towns with little picturesque cottages and some farm animals and beautiful views.
sentences.zh: 所以你是说像这种有着风景如画的小屋、一些农场动物和美丽景色的瑞士山地小镇。

sentences.en: Those are part of the defensive design.
sentences.zh: 那些也是防御性设计的一部分。

sentences.en: Not all of them, but yes, there's this whole subset of camouflage designs like anti-aircraft guns that are tucked behind these cute little windows
sentences.zh: 并非全部，但是的，这里有一整套伪装设计，比如藏在这些可爱的小窗户后面的防空炮

sentences.en: in cozy looking fake cottages.
sentences.zh: 藏在看起来很温馨的假小屋里。

sentences.en: And the juxtaposition is crazy.
sentences.zh: 这种并置太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Here, check out, check out this link.
sentences.zh: 来，看看，看看这个链接。

sentences.en: Just take, take a look.
sentences.zh: 看一看，看一看。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Oh my goodness.
sentences.zh: 噢天哪。

sentences.en: There's like a big gun coming out of the cottage.
sentences.zh: 就像有一门大炮从屋子里伸出来。

sentences.en: It is super strange, right?
sentences.zh: 超级奇怪，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, yeah.
sentences.zh: 就像，是的。

sentences.en: Whoa, that is really something.
sentences.zh: 哇，那真的很厉害。

sentences.en: That's a Swiss gun right there.
sentences.zh: 那可真是一门瑞士大炮。

sentences.en: It really is massive.
sentences.zh: 它确实非常巨大。

sentences.en: It's something else.
sentences.zh: 真是别具一格。

sentences.en: And what really is impressive to me too is the attention to detail on these things.
sentences.zh: 而且真正让我印象深刻的，是对这些东西的细节关注。

sentences.en: So in theory, these only really need to work at a distance, right?
sentences.zh: 所以按理说，这些东西实际上只需要在远距离起作用，对吧？

sentences.en: They're not made to be camouflaged up close, but nonetheless, they're really skillfully painted.
sentences.zh: 它们不是为了近距离伪装而制作的，但尽管如此，它们的绘制技术非常高超。

sentences.en: They even paint like fake shadows under the fake overhangs.
sentences.zh: 它们甚至在假悬挑下方画出假阴影。

sentences.en: You have to almost walk right up to one to see what they really are, or at least see what they're really not.
sentences.zh: 你几乎必须走到它跟前才能看出它们到底是什么，或者至少看出它们到底不是什么。

sentences.en: So it sounds like this approach kind of pervades all kinds of things in terms of their defensive design.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来这种方法在他们的防御性设计的方方面面都无处不在。

sentences.en: Like it has an effect on the architecture, the infrastructure, but, you know, is this a particularly Swiss thing?
sentences.zh: 就像它对建筑、基础设施产生了影响，但是，你知道，这是不是一个特别瑞士的特色？

sentences.en: I mean, is this where this kind of thing started?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种东西就是从这里开始的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, the Swiss have bunkers that, you know, date back to the 1800s, like most countries, but they got really worried and really serious about this stuff in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，瑞士有可以追溯到19世纪的掩体，就像大多数国家一样，但他们在20世纪30年代开始对这些东西感到非常担忧和严肃。

sentences.en: Wonder why.
sentences.zh: 难怪。

sentences.en: Yeah, right?
sentences.zh: 是吧？

sentences.en: So on the one hand, they had this relatively defensible, mountainous landscape, but on the other hand, they were completely surrounded by countries that, as it turned out,
sentences.zh: 所以一方面，他们拥有这种相对易守难攻的山地景观，但另一方面，他们完全被那些事实证明

sentences.en: were on the brink of another world war.
sentences.zh: 正处于又一次世界大战边缘的国家所包围。

sentences.en: So their preparations made sense.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的准备工作是有道理的。

sentences.en: So this kind of cropped up between those world wars, but you also mentioned the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 所以这种做法在两次世界大战之间涌现出来，但你也提到了冷战。

sentences.en: So it sounds like, you know, they got started, but then they saw kind of more of a need, even after the Axis and Allies powers, you know, fought all around them.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来，你知道的，他们开始了，但随后他们看到了更多需求，甚至在轴心国和同盟国力量在他们周围混战之后也是如此。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That like confirmed their suspicion that they really needed this kind of defense.
sentences.zh: 这证实了他们的怀疑，即他们确实需要这种防御。

sentences.en: And so Switzerland wanted to be prepared for anything and to make guerrilla war as hard as possible on potential enemies.
sentences.zh: 因此，瑞士希望为一切做好准备，并让潜在敌人的游击战变得尽可能困难。

sentences.en: So, among other things, they even built enough shelters to literally house the entire country's population, which it's unprecedented.
sentences.zh: 所以，除其他事项外，他们甚至建造了足够容纳整个国家人口的避难所，这前所未有。

sentences.en: No other nation has done anything like this.
sentences.zh: 没有其他国家做过类似的事情。

sentences.en: And it even became a matter of policy to make sure every citizen had the right to access bunker space if they needed it.
sentences.zh: 它甚至成了一项政策，确保每个公民在需要时都有权使用掩体空间。

sentences.en: Well, that's really something.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那真的很了不起。

sentences.en: And then there's all this self-destructive design, the big red button that blows everything up.
sentences.zh: 然后还有所有这些自我毁灭的设计，那个能炸毁一切的大红按钮。

sentences.en: I mean, it's hard to imagine, why have a button that destroys everything?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很难想象，为什么要有一个摧毁一切的按钮？

sentences.en: The emergency destruct system is now activated.
sentences.zh: 紧急自毁系统现已激活。

sentences.en: The ship will detonate in T-minus 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 飞船将在倒计时10分钟后自爆。

sentences.en: What circumstance makes you decide to really go through with that?
sentences.zh: 什么情况下会让你决定真正去执行它？

sentences.en: I mean, that's the crazy thing to me.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这对我来说才是最疯狂的。

sentences.en: And if you could imagine this from the point of view of an engineer, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你能从一个工程师的角度来想象这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: A Swiss engineer who is tasked with doing this.
sentences.zh: 一个负责这项工作的瑞士工程师。

sentences.en: So they're building a bridge.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在建一座桥。

sentences.en: They're building it to stand up and work as a bridge.
sentences.zh: 他们建造它是为了立起来并作为桥梁运作。

sentences.en: But they're simultaneously building it to blow up or to serve another function, right?
sentences.zh: 但他们同时也在建造它可以被炸毁或发挥其他功能的桥梁，对吧？

sentences.en: Like to be turned into a bunker or whatever.
sentences.zh: 比如变成一个掩体什么的。

sentences.en: And I actually read about this one bunker, for example, that is really just a railway tunnel that's used as a railway tunnel.
sentences.zh: 我实际上读到一个关于某个掩体的例子，它实际上只是一个用作铁路隧道的铁路隧道。

sentences.en: But they've packed it with supplies.
sentences.zh: 但里面塞满了物资。

sentences.en: And the idea is that in an emergency, they can house 20,000 people in there and they'd blow up and cave in the two main entrances.
sentences.zh: 这个想法是，在紧急情况下，他们可以在里面容纳两万人，并且他们会炸毁并塌陷两个主入口。

sentences.en: So it's like a rail tunnel by day.
sentences.zh: 所以它白天就像一个铁路隧道。

sentences.en: And then if disaster strikes, it can be this huge, like bunker that's carved into a mountain.
sentences.zh: 然后如果灾难降临，它就可以变成一个开凿在山里的巨大掩体。

sentences.en: The world has moved on like different.
sentences.zh: 世界已经发生了变化，变得不同了。

sentences.en: The Cold War has evolved in certain ways.
sentences.zh: 冷战在某些方面已经演变了。

sentences.en: Like, is this still a thing?
sentences.zh: 比如，这还是个事吗？

sentences.en: Are they still making things like this?
sentences.zh: 他们还在做这样的东西吗？

sentences.en: Like, is this as part of the Swiss mentality when it comes to building things to have this kind of defensive structures?
sentences.zh: 比如，建造这类防御性结构是否仍然是瑞士人建造东西时的心态的一部分？

sentences.en: I mean, it is in part.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，部分是的。

sentences.en: So they now have more publicly known structures and installations and bases and things.
sentences.zh: 所以他们现在有了更多为人所知的结构、设施、基地之类的东西。

sentences.en: But a lot of this stuff is still classified.
sentences.zh: 但很多这类东西仍然是保密的。

sentences.en: And so it's hard to tell exactly how much.
sentences.zh: 所以很难确切说出有多少。

sentences.en: But you can see this shift in that they've started to sell off some of these places.
sentences.zh: 但你可以看到这种转变，他们已经开始出售其中一些地方。

sentences.en: So, you know, there's some bunkers that people have turned into houses.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，有些人把一些掩体改造成了房子。

sentences.en: And also these fake homes that once housed artillery are now, in some cases, becoming real homes that house people.
sentences.zh: 而且这些曾经容纳火炮的假房屋现在在某些情况下正在变成容纳人们的真房屋。

sentences.en: I like that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: But that's something that we wrote about in the book with Toronto, the electric substations that were camouflaged as houses.
sentences.zh: 但我们在书里关于多伦多的内容中写过这一点，那些被伪装成房子的变电站。

sentences.en: And then the technology evolved past the point of needing these kind of converters.
sentences.zh: 然后技术发展到不再需要这种转换器的地步。

sentences.en: And therefore, those houses became actual houses.
sentences.zh: 因此，那些房子变成了真正的房子。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: It's a really strong parallel.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常强烈的平行对照。

sentences.en: And it's one of the reasons I was like, I thought about talking about this in the book.
sentences.zh: 这也是我当时想在书中讨论它的原因之一。

sentences.en: And that section was getting a little bit long on camouflage.
sentences.zh: 而且关于伪装的那一部分有点太长了。

sentences.en: So it felt a little redundant.
sentences.zh: 所以感觉有点重复。

sentences.en: Pretend to be a thing long enough.
sentences.zh: 假装成某样东西足够久。

sentences.en: Maybe you'll grow up to be that thing.
sentences.zh: 也许你就会长大成为那样东西。

sentences.en: When Pinocchio becomes a real boy.
sentences.zh: 当匹诺曹变成一个真正的男孩时。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Thank you, Kurt.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，库尔特。

sentences.en: Thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: We have one more mini story about the strange tax law that made ABBA dress the way they do.
sentences.zh: 我们还有一个关于奇怪税法的迷你故事，正是这个法律让ABBA变成了现在的穿着打扮。

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: After this.
sentences.zh: 广告之后。

sentences.zh: 接下来是制作人薇薇安·莱（Vivian Lay）。

sentences.en: Hey, Viv.
sentences.zh: 嘿，维夫。

sentences.en: Hey, Roman.
sentences.zh: 嘿，罗曼。

sentences.en: So what do you have for us this year?
sentences.zh: 所以今年你给我们带来了什么？

sentences.en: So what I wanted to do for my mini story this year is talk about the band ABBA because it's been a very long, very difficult year.
sentences.zh: 所以我今年想在我的迷你故事里谈谈ABBA这个乐队，因为这是一个非常漫长、非常艰难的一年。

sentences.en: And ABBA brings me a lot of joy.
sentences.zh: 而ABBA给我带来了很多欢乐。

sentences.en: I mean, did you have anything specific about ABBA or did you just want to chat about ABBA for the next 10 minutes?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你是有关于ABBA的具体内容，还是只是想在接下来的10分钟里聊聊ABBA？

sentences.en: I would actually love to chat about ABBA and the Mamma Mia cinematic universe and how much it rules.
sentences.zh: 我其实很想聊聊ABBA和《妈妈咪呀》的电影宇宙以及它有多么棒。

sentences.en: But I actually do have something specifically that I wanted to talk about.
sentences.zh: 但我确实有一些具体想谈的事情。

sentences.en: And that's ABBA's outfits.
sentences.zh: 那就是ABBA的服装。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Because I think it's pretty well documented that they consistently dressed in these outrageous stage costumes when performing.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得有充分的记录表明，他们在表演时一直穿着这些离谱的舞台服装。

sentences.en: Yeah, they were not known for their subtlety.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们可不是以低调闻名的。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: So I guess I'm just going to give you a quick tour of some of ABBA's best looks so that we could be on the same page.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我只是带大家快速参观一下ABBA的一些最佳造型，这样我们就能达成共识。

sentences.en: So I dropped in a photo, which is a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以我发了一张照片，内容很多。

sentences.en: It's a look.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个造型。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Yeah, indeed.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Frida, who's on the left, she's wearing a snakeskin jumpsuit.
sentences.zh: 所以弗里达在左边，她穿着一件蛇皮连身裤。

sentences.en: You've got Benny next door, who's wearing like this blue blazer and his lapels are made out of a giant like ostrich plume.
sentences.zh: 旁边是本尼，他穿着一件蓝色西装外套，翻领是用巨大的鸵鸟羽毛做成的。

sentences.en: But my favorite is Bjorn, who's on the very right.
sentences.zh: 但我最喜欢的是最右边的比约恩。

sentences.en: He's wearing a head to toe jumpsuit, blue, skin tight with a cape.
sentences.zh: 他穿着一身从头到脚的连身裤，蓝色，紧身，还带着斗篷。

sentences.en: I mean, they kind of look like professional wrestlers or kind of like circus performers or maybe circus performing professional wrestlers.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们看起来有点像职业摔跤手，或者有点像马戏团演员，或者可能是马戏团表演职业摔跤手。

sentences.en: Bjorn literally looks like he's about to be shot out of a cannon in this picture.
sentences.zh: 在这张照片里，比约恩看起来简直就像要被当成炮弹发射出去一样。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Oh, it's so good.
sentences.zh: 噢，太棒了。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: I love it so much.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: But like the reason why I want to talk about ABBA's fashion choices in particular is because I had read this really weird piece of trivia that, you know, if it's true,
sentences.zh: 不过我想聊聊阿巴乐队（ABBA）的时尚选择，原因是我读到过一个非常奇特的冷知识，你知道的，如果这是真的话，

sentences.en: makes this the perfect mini story for me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说简直是一个完美的小故事。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: The reason why ABBA's outfits were like so out there and so wild was because according to Swedish tax law at the time,
sentences.zh: 阿巴乐队的服装之所以那么出挑、那么疯狂，是因为根据当时瑞典的税法，

sentences.en: if you're a performer and your costumes were not suitable for everyday wear, they were tax deductible.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一名表演者，且你的演出服不适合日常穿著，它们就可以抵税。

sentences.en: That's so funny.
sentences.zh: 太搞笑了。

sentences.en: So the point is, is like if you're a musician and your stage clothes are just too impractical for everyday wear to go, you know, to a birthday party or an idea or something,
sentences.zh: 所以重点是，如果你是一个音乐人，你的舞台服装对于日常穿著来说实在太不实用了，比如去参加生日派对或约会什么的，

sentences.en: you could actually write them off like as costumes like they were professional wear.
sentences.zh: 你实际上可以把它们当作服装报销，就像它们是职业工装一样。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没准。

sentences.en: Like, so this had been picked up by a bunch of different websites, but it was reported that this particular tax law encouraged ABBA's costume designer to make their stage outfits,
sentences.zh: 这被很多不同的网站转载过，据报道称，正是这项特殊的税法鼓励了阿巴乐队的服装设计师，

sentences.en: you know, as flamboyant and essentially as unwearable as possible.
sentences.zh: 让他们的舞台服装，尽量做到华丽夺目且基本上无法日常穿著。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, this actually kind of reminds me of the fact that bricks were taxed differently in England at different times.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这其实让我想起了英国在不同时期对砖块征收不同的税。

sentences.en: And so you can sort of date how old a building is by the size of its bricks.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以通过砖块的大小来判断一座建筑有多老。

sentences.en: So there's all kinds of things in the, in the design world that are due to, you know, mundane tax considerations and not because of some grand design idea.
sentences.zh: 设计界有各种各样的事情都是由于世俗的税收考量，而不是因为什么宏大的设计理念。

sentences.en: But, but it does make me think, you know, in the case of how flamboyant these costumes are and because it's ABBA and because it's the internet, you know,
sentences.zh: 但是，这确实让我觉得，考虑到这些服装有多华丽，而且因为对象是阿巴乐队，又是在互联网上，

sentences.en: just like how much this is true versus how much this is just ABBA clickbait.
sentences.zh: 这其中有多少是事实，又有多少只是阿巴的点击诱饵。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: Cause this is still disco music that they are dressing for.
sentences.zh: 因为他们打扮的毕竟还是迪斯科音乐。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I got kind of hung up on this.
sentences.zh: 我有点对这件事耿耿于怀。

sentences.en: Um, so I ended up calling somebody to find out.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我最后给某个人打了电话想弄个明白。

sentences.en: Yes, Vivian, I'm with you.
sentences.zh: 对，薇薇安（Vivian），我和你在一起。

sentences.en: Hi, you know, it was me.
sentences.zh: 嗨，你知道的，那就是我。

sentences.en: Um, is, is now still a good time to talk?
sentences.zh: 嗯，现在还是聊天的好时机吗？

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: Nothing can take me away from you until death do us part.
sentences.zh: 直到死亡将我们分开，没什么能把我从你身边带走。

sentences.en: That's a charmer there, right there.
sentences.zh: 这话可真迷人。

sentences.en: Seriously.
sentences.zh: 说真的。

sentences.en: So who's this?
sentences.zh: 那这位是谁？

sentences.en: So this is Uwe Sandström.
sentences.zh: 这位是乌韦·桑德斯特伦（Uwe Sandström）。

sentences.en: My name is Uwe Sandström.
sentences.zh: 我叫乌韦·桑德斯特伦。

sentences.en: I am, um, well, among other things, the designer of the world famous ABBA group from Sweden.
sentences.zh: 嗯，除了别的身份之外，我还是来自瑞典的世界著名阿巴乐队的设计师。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So you, you, you went straight to the horse's mouth.
sentences.zh: 所以你直接去找了当事人。

sentences.en: This is the source.
sentences.zh: 这就是消息源。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: And I really wanted to talk to Uwe, not just because he knows the answer to this tax question, um,
sentences.zh: 我真的很想和乌韦聊聊，不仅仅是因为他知道这个税务问题的答案，

sentences.en: but also because he might literally have the most fascinating career on the planet.
sentences.zh: 还因为他可能拥有地球上最引人入胜的职业生涯。

sentences.en: I'm also professor of science, teaching young people to become zookeepers and working with wildlife and endangered species.
sentences.zh: 我其实还是一名理科教授，教年轻人成为动物管理员，并从事野生动物和濒危物种保护工作。

sentences.en: I'm actually also working as a safari guide in Kenya.
sentences.zh: 我实际上还在肯尼亚担任野生动物园向导。

sentences.en: I've been doing that for 25 years.
sentences.zh: 我干这个已经25年了。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: He's a, so he's a zoologist who leads safari tours in Kenya and also designed all the costumes for ABBA.
sentences.zh: 他是一个在肯尼亚带野生动物园旅行团的动物学家，同时还为阿巴设计了所有的服装。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he also arranges flowers, um, and he owns a restaurant, but probably the thing that he's really known for now is his work with endangered animals.
sentences.zh: 他还安排插花，嗯，他拥有一家餐厅，但可能他现在最广为人知的事迹是他在濒危动物保护方面的工作。

sentences.en: Um, he's actually one of those television animal specialists who will bring like tarantulas and tortoises onto talk shows.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他其实是那种会把狼蛛和陆龟带到脱口秀节目上的电视动物专家之一。

sentences.en: So he's basically like the Jack Hanna of Sweden.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上就像是瑞典的杰克·汉纳（Jack Hanna）。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全赞同。

sentences.en: I know exactly what you mean.
sentences.zh: 我完全明白你的意思。

sentences.en: He actually started out his career wanting to work with endangered animals and just kind of fell into costume design.
sentences.zh: 他的职业生涯其实是从想从事濒危动物工作开始的，只是阴差阳错地做起了服装设计。

sentences.en: So how does one do that?
sentences.zh: 那人怎么会做这个呢？

sentences.en: How does one go from working with animals to ABBA?
sentences.zh: 一个人怎么会从跟动物打交道转行到阿巴乐队？

sentences.en: Well, that's also kind of a wonky story.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这也是一个挺离奇的故事。

sentences.en: So according to Uwe, he was at university studying like zoology and botany and marine biology.
sentences.zh: 据乌韦说，他当时在大学里学习动物学、植物学和海洋生物学。

sentences.en: You see, studying at the university was quite expensive.
sentences.zh: 你看，在大学里学习是很贵的。

sentences.en: So I had to earn some money.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须赚点钱。

sentences.en: And you see, believe it or not, but during a period of my young life, I was studying the art of flamenco.
sentences.zh: 你看，信不信由你，在我年轻的一段时间里，我一直在学习弗拉门戈艺术。

sentences.en: Wait, flamenco dancing?
sentences.zh: 等等，弗拉门戈舞？

sentences.en: Is that what he said?
sentences.zh: 他是这么说的吗？

sentences.en: Yes, flamenco dancing.
sentences.zh: 对，弗拉门戈舞。

sentences.en: Okay, so let's, let's back up for people who just drew this.
sentences.zh: 好的，那我们倒回一点，给刚听到这的人理理。

sentences.en: He's a zoologist who leads safari tours in Africa.
sentences.zh: 他是一位在非洲带野生动物园旅行团的动物学家。

sentences.en: He designs costumes for ABBA and is also was a professional flamenco dancer.
sentences.zh: 他为阿巴设计服装，而且过去还是一名专业的弗拉门戈舞者。

sentences.en: Yes, he's literally the most fascinating person on the planet.
sentences.zh: 对，他简直是地球上最迷人的人。

sentences.en: So Uwe told me that he basically started sewing because he and his fiancee, you know, at the time, they had this background in flamenco dancing.
sentences.zh: 所以乌韦告诉我，他开始学做衣服基本上是因为他和当时的未婚妻都有弗拉门戈舞的背景。

sentences.en: And Uwe figured that they could earn some extra money by performing at flamenco clubs.
sentences.zh: 乌韦觉得他们可以通过在弗拉门戈俱乐部表演来赚点外快。

sentences.en: But there was this one problem, which was that his fiancee said that she didn't have any flamenco dresses to perform in.
sentences.zh: 但这里有一个问题，那就是他的未婚妻说她没有任何弗拉门戈裙子可以用来表演。

sentences.en: And I said, that's not a problem, darling.
sentences.zh: 我说，这不是问题，亲爱的。

sentences.en: I will make one for you.
sentences.zh: 我给你做一件。

sentences.en: And of course, she laughed.
sentences.zh: 当然，她笑了。

sentences.en: And she said, but you can't make flamenco dresses.
sentences.zh: 她说，但你不会做弗拉门戈裙子啊。

sentences.en: Uwe, come on.
sentences.zh: 乌韦，拜托。

sentences.en: It's quite complicated.
sentences.zh: 这挺复杂的。

sentences.en: And you see, you shouldn't say no to a person like me.
sentences.zh: 你看，你不该对像我这样的人说不。

sentences.en: So he ended up taking his mother's old dresses and then teaching himself how to make flamenco dresses.
sentences.zh: 所以他最后拿了他妈妈的旧裙子，然后自学了怎么做弗拉门戈裙子。

sentences.en: And he just ended up being like very naturally good at it.
sentences.zh: 结果他在这方面表现出了极高的天赋。

sentences.en: So the dresses that he was making for his fiancee caught the eye of a local theater group in the area.
sentences.zh: 所以他为未婚妻做的裙子吸引了当地一个剧团的目光。

sentences.en: So he started deciding for them.
sentences.zh: 于是他开始为他们设计。

sentences.en: And then he started working with, you know, local musical artists making costumes for like musical performers.
sentences.zh: 接着他开始与当地的音乐艺术家合作，为音乐表演者制作服装。

sentences.en: And that's how he ended up meeting Frida from ABBA.
sentences.zh: 这就是他如何结识阿巴乐队的弗里达（Frida）的。

sentences.en: So she took her friends, three of them and herself, of course, to my studio.
sentences.zh: 所以她带着她的三个朋友，当然还有她自己，来到了我的工作室。

sentences.en: And I said, well, tell me, tell me, friends.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，告诉我，朋友们。

sentences.en: I don't know anything about you.
sentences.zh: 我对你们一无所知。

sentences.en: Well, I know you've been singing and who you are, but what do you want?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我知道你们一直在唱歌，也知道你们是谁，但你们想要什么？

sentences.en: And then Vivian, then Vivian, Bjorn said these words.
sentences.zh: 然后，薇薇安，然后，比约恩（Bjorn）说了这样的话。

sentences.en: Remember them.
sentences.zh: 记住它们。

sentences.en: Uwe, remember, nothing is too wild.
sentences.zh: 乌韦，记住，没有什么太疯狂的。

sentences.en: I guarantee he did regret that many times.
sentences.zh: 我敢保证他后来后悔了很多次。

sentences.en: So the first outfit that he ended up designing for ABBA as a group was for this video called Ring Ring.
sentences.zh: 所以他为阿巴整个组合设计的第一套服装是一支名为《Ring Ring》的MV。

sentences.en: Those are actually the costumes from the picture that I showed you above where, you know, Frida's in the snakeskin jumpsuit and Bjorn's in that blue bodysuit with the cape.
sentences.zh: 那实际上就是我上面给你们看的照片里的服装，你知道的，弗里达穿着蛇皮连体裤，比约恩穿着那件带披风的蓝色紧身衣。

sentences.en: If you look at it, you can see Bjorn, he looks like something between a circus artist, a drag show and Superman.
sentences.zh: 如果你看一下，你会发现比约恩看起来介于马戏团演员、变装秀和超人之间。

sentences.en: He has a cape.
sentences.zh: 他有一件披风。

sentences.en: He has this leotard, you know, with big sequences, enormous platform shoes.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他穿着这件带有大亮片的紧身衣，还有巨大的恨天高。

sentences.en: Well, he looks really crazy because, you see, I was so fascinated by circus because I had some friends working with circus.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他看起来真的很疯狂，因为你看，我对马戏团太着迷了，因为我有一些朋友在马戏团工作。

sentences.en: And look at these outfits and costumes and you got a small circus company.
sentences.zh: 看看这些服装和行头，你就像一个小马戏团公司。

sentences.en: Really, it was the first time that a pop group should be dressed with plumes and with sequences and leotards and everything.
sentences.zh: 真的，这是流行乐队第一次穿著羽毛、亮片和紧身衣等各种行头亮相。

sentences.en: And that was the beginning.
sentences.zh: 这就是开端。

sentences.en: So what he's saying there is the reason why ABBA looked like they were straight out of the circus in that music video is because Uwe was literally inspired by the circus.
sentences.zh: 所以他当时的意思是，阿巴在那支音乐录影带里看起来像直接从马戏团出来的一样，是因为乌韦确实受到了马戏团的启发。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: It's a straight line.
sentences.zh: 这是一脉相承的。

sentences.en: Well, so I guess the big question is, is did the tax deduction incentive encourage Uwe to make their outfits even more absurd?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想最大的问题是，减税激励是否促使乌韦把他们的服装设计得更加荒谬？

sentences.en: That's a very funny story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的故事。

sentences.en: Well, it is actually partly, partly true, but not concerning ABBA.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这其实部分属实，但跟阿巴无关。

sentences.en: But can you imagine ABBA wearing these outfits when they're going shopping, singing, honey, honey, you want to buy some honey?
sentences.zh: 但你能想象阿巴穿着这些衣服去购物，唱着“亲爱的，亲爱的，你想买点蜂蜜吗？”

sentences.en: Yes, I want salad.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想买沙拉。

sentences.en: So he said that while he did purposefully make costumes more impractical for tax reasons for other musicians, that was never his goal when he was designing for ABBA.
sentences.zh: 所以他说，虽然他确实出于税务原因故意让其他音乐人的服装变得不那么实用，但他在为阿巴设计时从来都不是这个目的。

sentences.en: I had some artists who came to me because I made costumes for most of Swedish artists, really most of them.
sentences.zh: 有些艺术家来找我，因为我为大多数瑞典艺术家制作服装，真的可以说是绝大多数。

sentences.en: And some of them came,
sentences.zh: 其中有些人会来，

sentences.en: can you please write me paper to the tax authorities so you can convince them that this outfit is not suitable for wearing at a funeral or at a dinner sitting or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你能为我给税务部门写张纸条吗，这样你就能说服他们这套衣服不适合在葬礼、晚宴或任何场合穿。

sentences.en: So that happened three or four times.
sentences.zh: 这种情况发生过三四次。

sentences.en: So actually, it's partly true because there was a law, and it still is a law in Sweden.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，这部分是真的，因为当时有一条法律，现在瑞典也依然有这条法律。

sentences.en: But I can tell you, it was never any part of any of the costumes that are designed and produced for the ABBA group.
sentences.zh: 但我可以告诉你，它从来都不是为阿巴乐队设计和制作的任何服装的一部分。

sentences.en: Never, ever.
sentences.zh: 从来没有。

sentences.en: So now you've got the complete answer.
sentences.zh: 所以现在你得到了完整的答案。

sentences.en: So in the end, were ABBA's costumes tax deductible?
sentences.zh: 所以到头来，阿巴的服装可以抵税吗？

sentences.en: I mean, probably because they were clearly not.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，大概可以，因为它们显然不适合日常穿著。

sentences.en: Yeah, like seriously, like why not write them off?
sentences.zh: 对，说真的，为什么不报销呢？

sentences.en: They're not suitable for everyday use.
sentences.zh: 它们不适合日常使用。

sentences.en: But that wasn't a factor in how Uwe designed for the group.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是乌韦为这个组合进行设计时的考量因素。

sentences.en: Like, I know that the tax deduction story, you know, makes for a good story, but I kind of like his answer better.
sentences.zh: 我知道减税的故事是个好故事，但我更喜欢他的回答。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, he didn't create these bonkers outfits for ABBA because he needed to.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他为阿巴设计这些疯狂的服装并不是因为他必须这么做。

sentences.en: It's just because he wanted to.
sentences.zh: 只是因为他想这么做。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: Like, Uwe was telling me that his inspiration came from everything from like the animals that he worked with to Swedish flowers to his friends at the circus.
sentences.zh: 乌韦告诉我，他的灵感来自于一切，从他合作过的动物到瑞典的花朵，再到他在马戏团的朋友。

sentences.en: So what he created was really a reflection of his eclectic background.
sentences.zh: 所以他创作的作品确实是他丰富多元的背景的反映。

sentences.en: Yeah, he really does have an eclectic background.
sentences.zh: 是的，他的背景确实非常丰富多彩。

sentences.en: What a fascinating man.
sentences.zh: 多麽迷人的一位男士。

sentences.en: Oh, Vivian.
sentences.zh: 噢，薇薇安。

sentences.en: Well, that's great.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, thank you for solving that mystery that I didn't know I actually needed solved.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你解开了这个我甚至不知道需要被解开的谜团。

sentences.en: It was my pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: I did want to give a quick thank you to the ABBA Museum in Stockholm for connecting me with Uwe.
sentences.zh: 我确实要对斯德哥尔摩的阿巴博物馆将我和乌韦联系起来表示由衷的感谢。

sentences.en: Oh, that's great.
sentences.zh: 噢，太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, and thanks to Uwe, because that's probably the most interesting man we've had on our show.
sentences.zh: 还要感谢乌韦，因为这可能是我们节目中迎来的最有趣的人。

sentences.en: He's the most fascinating person I've ever talked to in my life.
sentences.zh: 他是我一生中交谈过的最迷人的人。

sentences.en: Thank you, Uwe.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，乌韦。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们。

sentences.en: If we don't hear from each other, a merry, merry, merry Christmas and a happy new year.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不再通话，祝大家圣诞快乐，新年快乐。

sentences.en: Or as we say within the family, happy new year, happy new year, as we say.
sentences.zh: 或者正如我们在家族里常说的，新年快乐，新年快乐。

sentences.en: Bye bye, Vivian.
sentences.zh: 再见，薇薇安。

sentences.en: We're going to be hearing more mini stories from the rest of the 99PI crew.
sentences.zh: 我们接下来将听到99PI团队其他成员带来的更多小故事。

sentences.en: As the first two episodes of 2021.
sentences.zh: 作为2021年的前两期节目。

sentences.en: Happy new year.
sentences.zh: 新年快乐。

sentences.en: As of the end of 2020, 99% Invisible is Katie Mingle, Kurt Kolstad, Delaney Hall, Emmett Fitzgerald,
sentences.zh: 截至2020年底，《99%隐形》（99% Invisible）的成员有凯蒂·明格（Katie Mingle）、库尔特·科尔stad（Kurt Kolstad）、德莱尼·霍尔（Delaney Hall）、埃米特·菲茨杰拉德（Emmett Fitzgerald）

sentences.en: Sean Rial, Joe Rosenberg, Vivian Lay, Sophia Klatzker, Chris Berube, Abby McDon, Christopher Johnson, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 肖恩·里亚尔、乔·罗森伯格、维维安·莱、索菲亚·克拉茨克、克里斯·贝鲁布、艾比·麦克唐、克里斯托弗·约翰逊，还有我，罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 KALW in San Francisco and produced on Radio Row in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山 91.7 KALW 电台的一个项目，制作于美丽的加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心广播街。

sentences.en: We are a member of Radiotopia from PRX, a collective of the best, most innovative shows in all of podcasting.
sentences.zh: 我们是 PRX 旗下 Radiotopia 的成员，这是一个汇集了播客界最优秀、最具创新性节目的联盟。

sentences.en: Discover, listen, and support them all at Radiotopia.fm.
sentences.zh: 请访问 Radiotopia.fm 发现、收听并支持他们。

sentences.en: You can find us and join discussions about the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Facebook 上找到我们并参与关于节目的讨论。

sentences.en: You can tweet at me, at Roman Mars, and the show at 99PI.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在推特上 @ 我（即 Roman Mars），也可以 @ 节目官号 99PI.org。

sentences.en: We're on Instagram and Reddit, too.
sentences.zh: 我们也在 Instagram 和 Reddit 上。

sentences.en: I bet you can still buy a last-minute copy of the 99% Invisible City just in time for Christmas if you act right now.
sentences.zh: 我敢说，如果你现在立刻行动，说不定还能在圣诞节前夕买到一本《99%隐形城市》作最后关头的礼物。

sentences.en: Get it at your local bookstore or by going to 99PI.org slash book.
sentences.zh: 请在当地书店购买，或访问 99PI.org/book。

sentences.en: I know that your daily habits have changed a lot this year, and for the people who have stayed with us listening from week to week,
sentences.zh: 我知道你们的日常生活今年发生了很大变化，对于那些每周坚持收听我们的听众，

sentences.en: I thank you.
sentences.zh: 我要说谢谢。

sentences.en: I am grateful, and I do hope you keep coming back.
sentences.zh: 我很感激，也希望你们能继续收听。

sentences.en: There is so much more good stuff in 2021.
sentences.zh: 2021年还有更多精彩的内容。

sentences.en: I cannot wait.
sentences.zh: 我简直迫不及待了。

sentences.en: Keep in touch at 99PI.org.
sentences.zh: 请通过 99PI.org 与我们保持联系。

sentences.en: Radiotopia.
sentences.zh: Radiotopia。
